co_sleeping_indian_mountain.blurb: Sleeping Indian Mountain is a bouldering-only zone near Buena Vista in Colorado's Arkansas Valley, at about 8,300 feet. The problems are divided among several separate zones: Moccasin Area, Loin Cloth Area, Backside Area, and the Trail and River Boulders, with Headdress and The Bowels adding smaller clusters. Some of the problems sit down near the Arkansas River. Difficulty runs from V0 to V9, with the main weight in the middle, V2 to V5, so it suits climbers working through intermediate grades as well as those ready to push higher. It is part of the larger bouldering scene east of Buena Vista, which holds most of the town's bouldering.

id_ross_park.blurb: Ross Park in Pocatello, Idaho, has two short basalt cliff areas: Sunny Side and Shady Side. Sunny Side holds compact bolted lines, with leads of just a few bolts and anchors set up for top-roping, and it bakes in afternoon sun in summer and early fall. Shady Side is a wall about 25 to 30 feet high and is friendly to families and newer climbers. Top-roping is the most common way to climb here, followed by sport leads, with a little bouldering on smaller walls. Grades run from about 5.7 to 5.12, centered on 5.9 and 5.10, and the boulder problems are mostly easy. Climbers tend to shift to Shady Side once midday heat arrives, and early morning, afternoon and evening all work.

qc_montagne_d_argent.blurb: Montagne d'Argent is a climbing and hiking park in La Conception, a few kilometres north of Saint-Jovite, in the Laurentides region of Quebec. Hiking trails pass the walls and lead to a lake in the middle of the mountain. Most routes are a single pitch, usually bolted, with a good number of trad lines too, and easy access to the tops makes top-roping simple. Grades run from easy 5.4 up to 5.13, with most between 5.8 and 5.10, so it works for people learning the ropes and for those stepping up. Grand Canyon is the biggest sector, followed by M & M and Le Fou, and winter ice climbing is part of the mix.

ca_snow_valley_bouldering.blurb: Snow Valley Bouldering is a large collection of boulders scattered on both sides of Highway 18, east of Running Springs in the San Bernardino Mountains, at around 6,100 feet. The rock is fairly coarse, which gives good friction, though holds can wear and break. Most boulders are short and landings are generally flat, so a couple of pads usually do the job. Difficulty is firmly on the easy side: a big share of problems are very easy to V1, with a spread from V2 up to V6 above. The hardest problems have grown dirty from lack of traffic. Snow Valley West is by far the largest zone, followed by Central and South, where pines around the boulders give some shade in summer.

co_mother_s_buttress.blurb: Mother's Buttress is the main trad cliff of Unaweep Canyon, in western Colorado along Highway 141 about half an hour south of Grand Junction, at roughly 7,200 feet. The canyon walls are metamorphic granite and gneiss, with continuous cracks, solid faces and steep unbroken rock. Trad dominates, with a small number of bolted lines, and grades run from easy up to 5.12, mostly between 5.8 and 5.11. Lower Mother's has single-pitch cracks from about 5.7 to 5.10, the alcove at Middle Mother's holds the canyon's best set of single-pitch 5.11s, and Upper Mother's has the multi-pitch climbing. Cave Buttress and Other Mothers add more. The canyon is quiet and lightly visited, and nearly any dry day can be a climbing day.

oh_whipps_ledges.blurb: Whipps Ledges is a small sandstone crag in Hinckley Reservation, part of Cleveland Metroparks in northeast Ohio. The rock is a quartz sandstone with a fragile outer shell, so it is best left alone for roughly two days after rain. The ledges stand about 20 to 50 feet high. Top-roping is the main activity, with plenty of bouldering and a handful of gear routes. Grades span from easy 5.3 up to 5.12, mostly 5.7 to 5.10, and the boulder problems run mostly V0 to V3 with a few much harder. Main Wall is the biggest face, with Island, Beer Can Alley and Isle of Many Faces nearby. The area gets a mix of sun, shade and wind.
